description:
ptr_in_ranges (runtime/src/heap/ref_io.rs:68) tests each pointer the collector examines against every from-space range in turn, so a collection on a heap with N grafted gifts is O(edges x N). cheney_forward_strict_bits uses it to skip static closures and the halt singletons; is_active_from_space_object uses it to tell a heap box from a stack slot for scalar refs. Nothing is sorted and nothing should be.

Invert the question, as BEAM's ErtsInYoungGen tests "not a literal and not in the old heap": under process isolation a heap-kinded pointer is either in from-space or in the static area, and a scalar ref's storage is either a heap box or a stack slot; to-space is new. Test the small fixed areas, so the chain's length enters no pointer test.

Done when:
- The collector's membership question is answered by a predicate over the static area (static closure table, halt singletons) and the stack extent, with from_ranges no longer consulted per pointer. ptr_in_ranges is deleted or survives only behind cfg(test) for the heap tests that assert ranges.
- A debug assertion (or the gc event's walked-ranges count from .1) shows the count is 0 after this change; the event field is deleted if it has nothing left to count.
- A heap unit test grafts many small gifts and collects, asserting every gift survivor is forwarded and every static closure is left in place.
- No fixture pin changes.
- Documentation in the same commit: every .agent/docs page, guide (guides/*.html), README.md section and fixture README that describes a mechanism this ticket changes or removes is rewritten to the present fact in the same commit, and a grep for the old names and phrases over .agent, guides, README.md and fixtures returns nothing. Full gate green (--workspace --all-targets plus doc tests, fixture matrix with --test-threads=1). Commit in Why / What changed / Verification form. No co-author trailer, no attribution line.

## Investigation 2026-11-08 (report: session scratchpad gl6/t4/investigation.md): the premise does not hold; awaiting the user's decision on scope

- Static closures and halt singletons are per-process 24-byte system allocations (process.rs:530-596, static_closure_bufs at :165), one set per spawn; deep_copy passes non-heap pointers through unchanged (deep_copy.rs:270-272), so a process's heap can hold pointers into ANOTHER process's static buffers. Nothing dangles today only because exited tasks stay in the registry. AOT children alias their parent's (aot_shim.rs:457,475).
- Static struct literals exist (.fz_static_struct_* data objects, native_codegen/prim.rs:169-258) with no exposed extent; their header flags word is always 0, so a static bit fits; closure headers have no spare bit.
- 'Stack extent' is vacuous: collection happens only at a quantum boundary and pinned scalars are heap-boxed; the real non-heap scalar storage is the Rust static NIL_ATOM_REF_SLOT (ir_runtime.rs:60) and interior slots of static structs.
- Heap::current_heap_tagged_addr / current_heap_addr_for_kind are dead code. GcStats.from_ranges_walked is from_ranges.len() (same as blocks_released), not a walk count, and should go.
- Cost: one collection of N three-cell lists grafted as N gifts vs one block: 100 = 2.7x, 1000 = 14x, 10000 = 127x (quadratic). Invisible at fixture scale; matters at thousands of grafted blocks.
- An exact inversion needs: one program-wide static closure slab (also fixes the cross-process pointer hazard), a static bit in the struct header, every scalar ref held at a boundary a heap box, and a debug cross-check against the ranges. Moved to the end of the epic (after .9) pending that decision.
title: A pointer's space is decided by testing the static area and the stack, not by walking the from-space chain
